query: FCC high-entropy alloys lose substantial strength above 800 °C, motivating refractory high-entropy alloys. Equal-atomic, single-phase BCC NbMoTaW retains excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but has poor room-temperature ductility, and its irradiation resistance has been inferred computationally rather than established here experimentally. Studies of other refractory high-entropy alloys have found greater irradiation resistance than pure tungsten under helium implantation and self-healing behavior associated with enhanced atomic diffusion and redistribution. However, irradiation-induced amorphization, helium-energy-dependent blistering, and irradiation-enhanced precipitation have also been observed, indicating unresolved phase- and surface-stability risks. Given the need to preserve BCC structural stability and high-temperature mechanical performance while improving room-temperature ductility and irradiation tolerance, what intervention could achieve this balance? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted directional or quantitative outcomes relative to untreated NbMoTaW, the applicable temperature and irradiation boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding HCP elements, specifically titanium, to the BCC NbMoTaW alloy will enhance its room-temperature ductility and irradiation tolerance while preserving its BCC structural stability and high-temperature mechanical performance.
generation.intervention: Composition change by adding 10 at.% titanium to form a (NbMoTaW)_{0.9}Ti_{0.1} alloy
generation.conditions: Up to 1600 °C, helium implantation with energies between 1 and 10 keV
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced configurational entropy due to the addition of HCP titanium
generation.mechanism: The introduction of titanium atoms into the BCC lattice will increase the configurational entropy, potentially reducing the driving force for irradiation-induced amorphization and enhancing atomic diffusion, which can mitigate helium-energy-dependent blistering and irradiation-enhanced precipitation.
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20% increase in room-temperature ductility and a 30% reduction in irradiation-induced hardness increase compared to untreated NbMoTaW
generation.boundary: Temperature: up to 1600 °C, Irradiation: helium implantation with energies between 1 and 10 keV
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of titanium to be added and the potential for titanium to form precipitates or alter the alloy's high-temperature mechanical properties are uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare (NbMoTaW)_{0.9}Ti_{0.1} and untreated NbMoTaW samples, conduct helium implantation at 5 keV, and measure the resulting microstructure, hardness, and ductility.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the (NbMoTaW)_{0.9}Ti_{0.1} alloy shows less than 10% increase in room-temperature ductility or more than 20% decrease in high-temperature mechanical performance compared to untreated NbMoTaW, the hypothesis is falsified.
